title: Petra’s ‘Treasury’ held no treasure, but its stone urn is scarred by bullet holes

cover.alt: Al-Khazneh at Petra: a tall façade of columns, pediments and a central urn carved directly into a rose-pink sandstone cliff.

body: Al-Khazneh, ‘the Treasury’, is the first façade visitors see on leaving the narrow Siq gorge at Petra in Jordan: about **39 m high** and 25 m wide, carved straight out of the sandstone cliff in Hellenistic style. It is thought to be a mausoleum from the early 1st century AD, in the reign of the Nabataean king Aretas IV. The name comes from Bedouin legend: the urn high on the façade was said to hold a pharaoh’s treasure, and the significant bullet damage on it is attributed to people who shot at the solid sandstone urn hoping to break it open. In 1989 the façade played the entrance to the Holy Grail’s hiding place in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade.

slides.alt: The carved façade of Al-Khazneh glimpsed through the narrow, shadowed cleft of the Siq gorge at Petra.
slides.caption: The first glimpse of Al-Khazneh, ‘the Treasury’, at the end of the Siq, the winding gorge that leads into Petra.

slides.question: How tall is the Treasury’s façade?
slides.explanation: About 39 m high and 25 m wide, cut from the cliff face. Its carvings include eagles, dancing Amazons and the twins Castor and Pollux.

slides.question: What was Al-Khazneh most likely built as?
slides.explanation: Scholars see it as a mausoleum carved in the early 1st century AD, in the reign of the Nabataean king Aretas IV. Nothing suggests it ever stored treasure.

slides.heading: Hollywood
slides.text: In Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade (1989) the façade stands in for the entrance to the Holy Grail’s resting place. The interior scenes were filmed far away, at Elstree Studios in England. Bedouins named the monument in the early 19th century; another of its names, Khaznat el-Far’oun, means ‘treasury of the pharaoh’.
